lore: A book of veins, alloys and quiet metal.
use: The Simple Ores chapter of the Simple Modpack guide: 33 pages about the ores, alloys and blocks of this mod, in your language. Craft the guide shapeless from a book and a crafting table.
secret: The chapter unlocks the first time you pick up raw gold. An old single guide turns into the modpack guide when you use it.

lore: {name}: silver that drifted to the edge of the world and stayed.
use: Generates in veins of 6 in the End stone of the outer islands (highlands, midlands, barrens, small islands). Needs an iron pickaxe and drops 2 to 6 silver nuggets; Fortune helps, Silk Touch keeps the ore.
secret: Silver you can farm after the dragon, with no deep mining. The ore block itself also smelts into a silver ingot.

lore: {name}: a dull, heavy vein that never shows itself in a cave wall.
use: Generates only in stone, 6 veins of 9 per chunk between Y 0 and 72, never touching air. Needs a stone pickaxe and drops 1 to 2 raw lead; Fortune helps, Silk Touch keeps the ore.
secret: You find it by digging, not by looking: like buried diamonds, a vein that would touch air is not placed. More common than silver, rarer than copper.

lore: {name}: the heavy metal of the stone layer, found again among the islands.
use: Generates in the End stone of the outer islands, 6 veins of 7 per chunk between Y 20 and 80, never touching air. Needs a stone pickaxe and drops 1 to 2 raw lead; Fortune helps, Silk Touch keeps the ore.
secret: Like the Overworld lead ore it hides inside the stone, so dig into an island instead of searching its edges.

lore: {name}: a hard, pale vein that keeps to the deep.
use: Generates only in deepslate, like diamond ore: 10 veins of 6 per chunk, most at Y -64, up to Y 16. Needs an iron pickaxe and drops raw nickel; Fortune helps, Silk Touch keeps the ore.
secret: A little more common than diamond, because nickel is an ingredient, not a gear tier: one nickel and three iron ingots make four stainless steel.

lore: {name}: the mountain metal, at home where granite meets the sky.
use: Generates in stone and granite between Y 20 and 80, in dense nests inside granite, and up to Y 180 in the mountain biomes. Needs a stone pickaxe and drops raw tin; Fortune helps, Silk Touch keeps the ore.
secret: Look for granite: where a vein meets a granite blob, the tin crowds together. Rivers and beaches hide tin-bearing gravel and sand under water.

lore: {name}: one blushing stone in a vein of gold, deep down in the heat.
use: Hides in the Vanilla Nether gold veins below Y 31: each gold ore block has a 2 percent chance (server setting) to be this ore instead, at most one per vein. Iron pickaxe. Drops a Rose Gold Pressling; Fortune helps, Silk Touch keeps the ore.
secret: The pressling goes straight into the blast furnace, and the ore block itself melts into a rose gold ingot. Piglins get angry when you mine it, as with gold ore.

lore: The shell around a hidden heart of zinc.
use: The shell of the zinc mini geodes in the Overworld and their lining in the End. Any pickaxe mines it and it drops itself; a building block like smooth basalt.
secret: Find a ball of it in solid stone and dig in: behind a calcite lining wait 1 to 8 zinc ores.

lore: {name}: heavy, grey and deaf to the world on the other side.
use: Nine lead ingots make one, and it gives the nine back. Hardness 25, blast resistance 1000 (obsidian 1200), needs an iron pickaxe. Sculk sensors and the Warden do not hear through it, and every lead block on the way muffles sound behind it.
secret: It is loud itself: whoever walks on it or mines it makes noise. A TNT blast behind 3 lead blocks arrives at an eighth of its volume. Records stay unmuffled unless the server says otherwise.

lore: A slab of lead thin enough to hang on a wall.
use: Three lead ingots in a row make 6. It lies on the side you click, flat or upright; another plate on its free side stacks it like snow, 1 to 8 layers of 2 pixels. Breaking gives one plate per layer. Iron pickaxe.
secret: One layer muffles sound like half a block of lead, eight like a whole block. It stops no vibrations, and 8 plates never turn into a block.

lore: A sheet of silver so thin it is barely there.
use: Three silver ingots in a row make 12. It lies on the side you click (floor, wall or ceiling); another sheet on its free side adds a layer, up to 8 layers of one pixel. Breaking gives one sheet per layer. Iron pickaxe.
secret: A sheet and a glass pane, shapeless, make the Silver Mirror. Eight layers are only half a block: the same metal per pixel as lead plates.

lore: A silver frame round a pane of glass, for those who like to look twice.
use: A glass pane and a silver sheet, shapeless. It hangs on a wall or lies on the floor or the ceiling like a button, one pixel thick, and falls off when its support goes.
secret: It has no mechanic at all: pure decoration. On the floor or the ceiling it turns the way you look.

lore: A pale bar that rings like a small bell.
use: Smelted from raw silver or silver ore; nine nuggets make one too. Nine make a block. Every rose gold pressling needs one, and silver builds bars, grates, doors, lamps, sheets and the mirror.
secret: Silver is no tool material, and it is the bottleneck of rose gold: every pressling takes one, whichever alloy you press.

lore: A grey bar, heavier than it looks.
use: Smelted from raw lead or lead ore. Nine make a block of lead; three in a row make 6 lead plates. Lead builds bars, grates, doors and the soundproof building blocks.
secret: Lead blocks between a sound and your ear make it quieter: three of them swallow most of a TNT blast.

lore: A bluish-grey bar from the heart of a geode.
use: Smelted from raw zinc or zinc ore. Nine make a block. Two copper and one zinc ingot, shapeless, make 3 brass: nothing is lost.
secret: Zinc comes only from closed mini geodes, so every ingot started inside a ball of geode crust.

lore: A hard, bright bar from the deep.
use: Smelted from raw nickel or nickel ore. Nine make a block. Three iron and one nickel ingot, shapeless, make 4 stainless steel.
secret: One nickel stretches three iron into four ingots of steel, which is why nickel is only a little more common than diamond.

lore: A soft bar of the mountain metal.
use: Smelted from raw tin or tin ore; nine tin nuggets make one too. Nine make a block. Three copper and one tin ingot, shapeless, make 4 bronze.
secret: Tin crackles: its blocks make their own crackling tin cry when you walk on them or mine them.

lore: A warm yellow bar of copper and zinc.
use: Two copper and one zinc ingot, shapeless, make 3: nothing is lost. Nine make a block of brass. Brass builds bars, grates, doors, lamps, lanterns, chains and poles.
secret: Brass never oxidises, so it keeps the shine copper loses. Its grate pattern is made of rhombs.

lore: A hard bar of iron that refuses to rust.
use: Three iron and one nickel ingot, shapeless, make 4: nothing is lost. Nine make a block of stainless steel, the base of a whole building family.
secret: Its blocks have a hard, clean sound of their own. Like every metal of this mod it never ages.

lore: A warm brown bar, the oldest alloy of all.
use: Three copper and one tin ingot, shapeless, make 4: nothing is lost. Nine make a block of bronze, the base of its building family.
secret: Bronze sounds warm when you walk on it, and it does not oxidise: a bronze wall stays brown.

lore: A pale pink bar of gold, copper and silver.
use: Press 1 gold, 2 copper and 1 silver ingot into a Rose Gold Pressling (shapeless), then melt it in a blast furnace (30 s) for one ingot. Nine make a block. Tools, armor, apples and building blocks use it.
secret: It is the better alloy: tools as fast as gold with nearly iron durability, armor that lasts like iron. It is also an ingredient of Rose Copper.

lore: A darker copper-rose bar, rose gold with more gold in it.
use: Press 2 gold, 1 Rose Gold and 1 silver ingot into a Rose Copper Pressling (shapeless), then melt it in a blast furnace (30 s) for one ingot. Nine make a block. Tools, armor, apples and building blocks use it.
secret: Despite the richer recipe its gear is the weaker one: durability 190, like copper. Choose it for its darker color.

lore: Earth that went through the rift and came back as metal.
use: 4 Rift Shards and 1 Enderite ingot, shapeless. Nine make a block, a beacon base, and the ingot pays a beacon. Fire resistant, Legendary rank.
secret: It is the partner of the next step: 4 Nether Rift Shards and a Terranite ingot make Infernite. Its apple and carrot give Haste.

lore: A bar that kept the Nether's heat inside.
use: 4 Nether Rift Shards and 1 Terranite ingot, shapeless. Nine make a block, a beacon base, and the ingot pays a beacon. Fire resistant, Legendary rank.
secret: It is the partner of the last step: 4 End Rift Shards and an Infernite ingot make Zenithite. Its apple and carrot give Fire Resistance.

lore: The end of the chain, a bar as light as the sky above the islands.
use: 4 End Rift Shards and 1 Infernite ingot, shapeless. Nine make a block, a beacon base, and the ingot pays a beacon. Fire resistant, Legendary rank.
secret: Every dimension is in it: Overworld, Nether and End scrap and the Enderite at the start. Its apple and carrot give Slow Falling.

lore: Forged where the End forgets its own edges: the tier above netherite.
use: Four Enderite Scrap, four diamonds and a netherite ingot make one; nine nuggets make one too. Nine make a block. With the Enderite Upgrade it lifts netherite gear to Enderite at the smithing table.
secret: It also starts the rift alloys: 4 Rift Shards and an Enderite ingot make Terranite. Other Simple mods load their Enderite recipes only while Simple Ores is installed.

lore: A tiny piece of the End's heaviest metal, small enough to hide.
use: Nine make an Enderite ingot, and the ingot gives nine back. Eight round an apple make the Enderite Apple, four round a carrot the Enderite Carrot.
secret: End city treasure sometimes holds 2 to 5 of them, a head start toward your first ingot.

lore: A fragment of the End's own ore, still rough from the dark.
use: Found in End city treasure, 1 to 2 at a time. Four fragments, shapeless, make Raw Enderite Scrap, the first step toward Enderite.
secret: That scrap melts only in a blast furnace, and slowly. With SimpleBuilding installed the fragments can also be made by its synthesis.

lore: Raw Enderite, pressed in layers, ready for a long fire.
use: Four Raw Enderite Fragments, shapeless. Only a blast furnace melts it into Enderite Scrap, and it takes hours there; a furnace refuses it.
secret: Start the blast furnace before a long trip. Four scrap, four diamonds and a netherite ingot then make an Enderite ingot.

lore: What is left when the End's raw ore meets the fire and loses its illusions.
use: Melted from Raw Enderite Scrap in a blast furnace; End city treasure also holds it (15 percent). Four scrap, four diamonds and a netherite ingot make an Enderite ingot.
secret: Nine pack into a Block of Enderite Scrap, as hard as ancient debris and safe from fire.

lore: A template stamped with the End's own seal.
use: Smithing template: with a netherite tool, armor piece, mount armor or pole and an Enderite ingot it makes the Enderite version. Found in End city treasure (30 percent).
secret: Seven diamonds round it and an End stone copy it: one template becomes two, so you never need to hunt for more.

lore: Nine ingots of the End, folded into a cube: the heaviest thing a builder can own.
use: Nine Enderite ingots make one, and it gives the nine back. Needs a diamond pickaxe; it is a beacon base block.
secret: The stonecutter cuts it into Chiseled Enderite with an Eye of Ender motif. On its own Enderite is a treasure for building; its gear comes from the smithing table.

lore: Thought, grown into a clear stone the size of an ingot.
use: Four sage crystal shards in a square make one; nine make a block of sage crystal, and back. It counts as an ingot (tag c:ingots/sage_crystal).
secret: It has no use of its own yet: a material waiting for its purpose. The shards come from the Nether and End sage ores.

lore: A splinter of crystallised wisdom.
use: Dropped by the Nether and End sage ores, 1 to 3 at a time (Fortune helps). Four in a square make a sage crystal.
secret: The Overworld sage ore gives experience and orbs instead; only the ores of the other dimensions grow shards.

lore: Nine crystals of wisdom set into one block.
use: Nine sage crystals make one, and it gives the nine back. A storage and decoration block.
secret: The crystals inside have no further use yet, so the block is the nicest way to show them off.

lore: A pearl of stored thought, small enough to hold in one hand.
use: Right-click charges it for 0.3 seconds, then it gives 50 to 100 experience points and is used up.
secret: Sage ore sometimes drops one: 2 percent, up to 5 with Fortune. Nine pack into a block of sage orbs for safe keeping.

lore: A block of stored experience, waiting for a reader.
use: Nine sage orbs make one, and it gives the nine back. Needs an iron pickaxe.
secret: The block itself gives no experience: unpack it and use the orbs one by one, 50 to 100 points each.

lore: Four ingots squeezed together, waiting for the fire.
use: 1 gold, 2 copper and 1 silver ingot, shapeless, make 1. Only a blast furnace melts it (30 s), always into exactly 1 Rose Gold ingot; a furnace, smoker or campfire refuses.
secret: Four ingots in, one out: silver stays the bottleneck. Nether Rose Gold Ore drops a pressling directly.

lore: Gold, rose gold and silver pressed into one lump.
use: 2 gold, 1 Rose Gold and 1 silver ingot, shapeless, make 1. Only a blast furnace melts it (30 s), always into exactly 1 Rose Copper ingot; a furnace, smoker or campfire refuses.
secret: You need rose gold first: Rose Copper is made from it. Nine presslings pack into a block, but only single presslings melt.

lore: A golden apple with a pale pink blush.
use: 8 Rose Gold ingots round an apple. 6 hunger, always edible. Regeneration II 0:05, Absorption I 2:00, Resistance I 0:50.
secret: A step between the golden and the netherite apple: the golden apple's effects plus Resistance, but no Fire Resistance.

lore: An apple in a copper-rose coat.
use: 8 Rose Copper ingots round an apple. 5 hunger, always edible. Regeneration II 0:05, Absorption I 2:00, Resistance I 0:30.
secret: The Rose Gold apple fills one point more and its Resistance lasts longer (0:50). Neither gives Fire Resistance.

lore: {name}: a rose gold apple that kept the glow.
use: 8 blocks of Rose Gold round an apple. 6 hunger, always edible. Regeneration II 0:35, Resistance I 5:00, Fire Resistance 5:00, Absorption IV 2:00.
secret: It works like the enchanted golden apple, but you can craft it. The tooltip lists every effect.

lore: {name}: copper-rose, with a glint.
use: 8 blocks of Rose Copper round an apple. 5 hunger, always edible. Regeneration II 0:30, Resistance I 5:00, Fire Resistance 5:00, Absorption IV 2:00.
secret: Five seconds less Regeneration and one hunger point less than the enchanted Rose Gold apple, otherwise the same.

lore: {name}: a golden apple that went through the Nether and came back harder.
use: An apple ringed by 8 netherite nuggets. 8 hunger, always edible. Resistance I (1:00), Absorption II (0:30), Regeneration II (0:10).
secret: It is fire resistant as an item, so a drop into lava does not destroy it.

lore: {name}: a netherite apple that was given a glow and kept it.
use: It has no recipe: a rare loot find. 8 hunger, always edible. Regeneration II (0:40), Resistance I (5:00), Fire Resistance (5:00), Absorption IV (2:00), Strength II (2:00).
secret: Stronger than the plain netherite apple in every effect, rare in rank, and fire resistant as an item.

lore: {name}: an apple with the End's patience in its skin.
use: An apple ringed by 8 Enderite nuggets. 14 hunger, always edible. Regeneration II (0:20), Resistance I (2:30), Absorption IV (2:00), Health Boost III (2:00).
secret: Epic rarity, fire resistant and safe from the void if dropped, like every Enderite item.

lore: {name}: the End has only one fruit like it.
use: It has no recipe: a rare loot find. 14 hunger, always edible. Regeneration III (1:00), Resistance II (5:00), Fire Resistance (10:00), Absorption V (3:00), Health Boost V (3:00), Night Vision (5:00).
secret: Epic, with an enchantment glint, and fire resistant like every Enderite item.

lore: {name}: a carrot that got serious.
use: A carrot with 4 netherite nuggets around it in a plus. 6 hunger, always edible. Fire Resistance (2:00) and Night Vision (2:00).
secret: A snack for the Nether: two minutes of seeing in the dark and not burning. It is fire resistant as an item.

lore: {name}: a carrot that learned to jump between islands.
use: A carrot with 4 Enderite nuggets around it in a plus. 12 hunger, always edible. Night Vision (5:00), Speed II (1:00), Jump Boost II (1:00) and a tick of Saturation.
secret: Epic, fire resistant and safe from the void, like every Enderite item.

lore: A pole of iron, thin, straight and eager to be struck by something.
use: Three iron ingots stacked make one. A lightning rod of iron: it draws strikes within 32 blocks as the top block of its column and gives a redstone signal when struck. Stone pickaxe.
secret: A copper lightning rod in reach always goes first. Among metal poles the nearest one wins the strike.

lore: A pole of gold: too soft for work, too shining to hide.
use: Three gold ingots stacked make one. A lightning rod of gold that draws strikes within 64 blocks and gives a redstone signal when struck. Needs an iron pickaxe.
secret: Poles come in tiers: iron 32, gold 64, emerald 72, diamond 80, netherite 96 and enderite 128 blocks.

lore: A pole of emerald, green as a trade gone well.
use: Three emeralds stacked make one. A lightning pole that draws strikes within 72 blocks, unless a copper lightning rod is in reach. Needs an iron pickaxe.
secret: It sits between gold (64) and diamond (80). When several poles reach a strike, the nearest one wins.

lore: A pole of diamond, too precious to stand in a storm, which is exactly where it wants to be.
use: Three diamonds stacked make one: a lightning rod of diamond that draws strikes within 80 blocks. With the Netherite Upgrade and a netherite ingot the smithing table turns it into the Netherite Pole.
secret: Like every metal pole it never oxidises and gives a redstone signal when lightning strikes it.

lore: A pole that has stood in the fire and does not mind the next one.
use: Smithing table: Netherite Upgrade, Diamond Pole and netherite ingot give the Netherite Pole, a lightning rod that draws strikes within 96 blocks. Needs a diamond pickaxe.
secret: It does not burn, and with the Enderite Upgrade it becomes the Enderite Pole, one tier up.

lore: A pole that remembers the sky and draws lightning like a promise.
use: Smithing table: Enderite Upgrade, Netherite Pole and Enderite ingot give the Enderite Pole, a lightning rod that draws strikes within 128 blocks. Needs a diamond pickaxe.
secret: It reaches as far as the copper rod, but copper still goes first. Fire resistant and safe from the void like every Enderite item.

lore: It waits on the very top of the End's islands, and glints at anyone with a good pickaxe.
use: Generates in the End stone on the surface of the outer islands. Diamond pickaxe or better, hardness 20, light level 5. Drops Astralit Dust and 3 to 7 experience; Fortune raises the drop, Silk Touch keeps the ore.
secret: It hides in the stone until a brush frees it: six strokes show its crystals. A freed ore drops its full amount, a hidden one only with a 70 percent chance.

lore: It hangs under the End's islands like a bruise in the dark.
use: Generates in the End stone on the underside of the islands. Diamond pickaxe or better, hardness 25. Drops a Nihilit Shard and 3 to 7 experience; Fortune raises the drop, Silk Touch keeps the ore.
secret: Look down, not up: the veins hang from the underside of the islands. Brush it free first (six strokes), or it drops its shard only with a 70 percent chance.

lore: A pink dust that drifts off the End's outer islands, still warm from the light it carries.
use: Dropped by Astralit Ore (Fortune adds more); four Dull Astralit Dust craft one too. With redstone it makes 2 Astral Redstone, with a Nihilit Shard and redstone 3 Bridge Redstone. A blaze rod over it makes 4 Astralit End Rods.
secret: With SimpleBuilding installed it is also a trim material and the base of the Astralit building blocks.

lore: A blue splinter of the void, cold like a held breath.
use: Dropped by Nihilit Ore (Fortune adds more); four Dull Nihilit Shards craft one too. With redstone it makes 2 Nihil Redstone, with Astralit Dust and redstone 3 Bridge Redstone. A blaze rod over it makes 4 Nihilit End Rods.
secret: It is also the heart of the Nihil Core. With SimpleBuilding installed it becomes a trim material and the base of the Nihilit building blocks.

lore: Redstone that has learned a second language, and speaks it only to its own kind.
use: Astralit Dust and redstone make 2. A second redstone line: it behaves like redstone dust, but dust only takes signal from dust of its own line. Lamps, pistons, doors and other devices react to every line.
secret: Used on the side or the underside of a block it sticks to that face and powers its block strongly. Bridge Redstone links it to the other lines.

lore: Redstone from the other side of the void, quiet and cold.
use: A Nihilit Shard and redstone make 2. A third redstone line: it behaves like redstone dust, but never takes signal from redstone or Astral dust. Lamps, pistons, doors and other devices react to every line.
secret: Two lines can run side by side without crosstalk. Only Bridge Redstone passes a signal from the dust of one line into another.

lore: Redstone that learned to translate between three tongues.
use: Astralit Dust, a Nihilit Shard and redstone make 3. It connects to redstone, Astral and Nihil dust alike and passes the signal on like one shared wire, one level weaker per block.
secret: Redstone dust reads a bridge only from the side next to it, not across a slope. Like Astral Redstone it also sticks to walls and ceilings.

lore: {name} pushes when the other side tells it to.
use: A piston, 4 Astral Redstone and 4 corners (Polished Astralit with SimpleBuilding, End stone bricks without). On a rising signal of any line it pushes the block on each of its six sides one cell away.
secret: One block per side, never a chain, and only into a free cell. It fires on the rising edge only, then waits 8 ticks (server setting).

lore: {name} pulls what waits one step away.
use: A sticky piston, 4 Nihil Redstone and 4 corners (Polished Nihilit with SimpleBuilding, End stone bricks without). On a rising signal of any line it pulls the block two cells away on each side into the cell next to it.
secret: A block already touching it stays put, and glazed terracotta can be pushed but not pulled. It fires once per rising edge, then waits 8 ticks.

lore: A rail that has heard the sky and wants to go there.
use: Six gold ingots, a stick and Astral Redstone make 6. Straight only. Powered by any redstone line, it pushes carts to a top speed of 16 blocks per second by default (Vanilla 8). Unpowered it is a plain rail.
secret: The boost fades the closer a cart gets to top speed. On slopes, in water and on other rails the Vanilla limit applies again, so brake before a curve.

lore: A rail that takes the speed out of the world, politely and completely.
use: Six gold ingots, a stick and Nihil Redstone make 6. Straight only. Powered by any redstone line, it brakes: each tick the cart keeps 80 percent of its speed minus a small amount, stops, and is held while the power stays on.
secret: Unpowered it lets carts roll through. A neighboring rail never powers it, so you can build a station that brakes on a signal.

lore: A copper bulb that learned to speak.
use: A copper bulb surrounded by four Astral Redstone. A rising signal edge toggles it; while on it lights up and gives redstone strength 15 to every side.
secret: A comparator reads 15 from it while it is on, so one pulse turns it into a steady source until the next pulse.

lore: Many cores, one thought.
use: A Nihilit Shard, four Nihil Redstone and four End stone bricks make 4. Touching cores form one group: a rising edge at any core toggles the whole group, and while on every core gives strength 15 to all sides.
secret: Neighboring cores draw one surface with a rim only around the outside, so a wall of cores looks like a single panel.

lore: {name}: a pale glint in the stone, rarer than gold and quieter about it.
use: Generates in 1 to 2 veins of 5 per chunk between Y -48 and 16, in stone and deepslate. Needs an iron pickaxe and drops raw silver; Fortune raises the drop, Silk Touch keeps the ore.
secret: Silver is no tool metal: it goes into rose gold and building blocks. After the dragon, the End silver ore on the outer islands is the easier source.

lore: {name}: a grey heart inside a closed stone shell.
use: Zinc has no free veins: it grows only in closed mini geodes, 1 to 8 ores in the core. Overworld geodes (Y -56 to 40) have a geode crust shell and a calcite lining, End ones an End stone shell and a geode crust lining. Stone pickaxe; drops raw zinc.
secret: A geode is placed only where it is fully enclosed, so it never shows in a cave. Fortune helps, Silk Touch keeps the ore.

lore: {name}: a riverbed that carries a little tin in every handful.
use: Rare small patches under water in river and beach beds, about one in every 3rd chunk of those biomes. It falls like its plain block. A shovel digs it for 2 to 5 tin nuggets; Fortune helps, Silk Touch keeps the block.
secret: Nine of those nuggets make a tin ingot, so a few patches give you bronze without a single pickaxe swing.

lore: {name}: a vein that holds knowledge and gives it up reluctantly.
use: Generates in the Overworld as rarely as diamond ore. Needs an iron pickaxe and drops 3 to 7 experience and rarely a sage orb: 2 percent, up to 5 with Fortune. Silk Touch keeps the ore but gives no experience.
secret: The orb is stored experience: right-click charges it for 0.3 seconds, then it gives 50 to 100 points.

lore: {name}: wisdom that wandered off into another dimension.
use: Nether: in netherrack, 5 veins of 4 per chunk. End: in End stone on the outer islands, 3 veins of 4 per chunk. Iron pickaxe. Drops 1 to 3 sage crystal shards and 2 to 5 experience; Fortune helps, Silk Touch keeps the ore.
secret: Four shards in a square make a sage crystal, the ingot-sized material of the sage family. The server switch sageOreOtherDimensions turns both ores off.

lore: {name}: the same vein, only milky and without a glint.
use: About one block in five of every Astralit or Nihilit vein is dull. Diamond pickaxe; drops 1 to 3 experience and the dull dust or shard (Fortune helps, Silk Touch keeps the block). Dull Astralit Ore glows at light level 3.
secret: The brush does nothing on dull ores, and ore detectors ignore them. Four dull pieces still craft one real dust or shard.

lore: {name}: the unrefined cousin of the real thing.
use: Dropped by the dull ore of its kind (Fortune works like on the real ore). Four of them, shapeless, craft one real Astralit Dust or Nihilit Shard.
secret: Keep them: the dull blocks of a vein add up, and every fourth piece becomes a real one.

lore: {name}: a block found in every dimension, and in none of them quite at home.
use: Rarer than ancient debris: one vein of up to 2 in every 3rd chunk, never at air; deep in Overworld deepslate, in the Nether like ancient debris, inside the End islands. Only an Enderite pickaxe or sledgehammer breaks it (250 s unenchanted).
secret: It survives the Wither and the dragon, and no piston moves it. A blast furnace melts it into rift shards (Overworld 40 s, Nether 60 s, End 80 s); a crucible only at extreme heat.

lore: {name}: shards of a dimension packed tight, like scrap waiting for a smith.
use: Nine shards make one, and it gives the nine back. Hard like ancient debris, fire resistant, needs a diamond pickaxe.
secret: It is storage, nothing more: the shards inside wait for the alloy chain from Terranite to Zenithite.

lore: {name}: what is left of a dimension once the fire has had its say.
use: Melted from the Dimensional Scrap of its dimension, only in a blast furnace or in a crucible at extreme heat; one scrap gives one shard. Nine make a block of shards. Fire resistant.
secret: The chain: 4 Rift Shards and an Enderite ingot make Terranite, 4 Nether Rift Shards and a Terranite ingot Infernite, 4 End Rift Shards and an Infernite ingot Zenithite.

lore: {name}: nine pieces of hard-won scrap in one heavy cube.
use: Nine scrap make one, and it gives the nine back. Like ancient debris: hardness 30, blast resistance 1200, fire resistant, needs a diamond pickaxe.
secret: A compact way to carry scrap home: a stack of blocks holds 576 scrap and does not burn in lava.

lore: {name}: a load of ore-rough metal, packed for the long way home.
use: Nine raw pieces make one, and it gives the nine back. A compact way to store raw metal before smelting.
secret: Unpack it in the crafting grid to smelt the nine raw pieces: the furnace does not take the block.

lore: {name}: metal as the ground gave it, still rough at the edges.
use: Mined from its ore (Fortune gives more). A furnace or blast furnace smelts it into an ingot. Nine make a block of the raw metal, and the block gives nine back.
secret: The ore block itself smelts as well, so Silk Touch only costs you the Fortune bonus.

lore: {name}: nine presslings stacked and waiting.
use: Nine presslings make one, and it gives the nine back. Needs an iron pickaxe.
secret: Storage only: the blast furnace does not melt the block, so unpack it and melt single presslings.

lore: {name}: nine ingots of a dimension's metal, a showpiece for a beacon.
use: Nine ingots make one, and it gives the nine back. A beacon base like the Enderite block; needs a diamond pickaxe, fire resistant.
secret: The stonecutter cuts it 1:1 into its chiseled block with a tree, a Ghast or a sun. That one is decoration only, no beacon base.
Lead stays lead, but only half: a cut lead stair or slab muffles sound like half a block of lead. It keeps the hardness 25 and blast resistance 1000 of the block.
Lead stays lead: like the block of lead it muffles sound, stops vibrations and keeps hardness 25 and blast resistance 1000.

lore: {name}: nine ingots, quiet and square, the start of a whole family of building blocks.
use: Nine ingots make one, and it gives the nine back. It is the base of its building family: cut blocks, stairs, slabs, tiles, pillar and chiseled block come from it at the crafting table or the stonecutter.
secret: Unlike copper it never oxidises and needs no wax, so a wall of it keeps its color forever.

lore: {name}: metal panels laid out step by step, or half a block high.
use: Six cut blocks in a stair shape make 4 stairs, three in a row make 6 slabs. The stonecutter cuts 4 stairs or 8 slabs from one storage block, or 1 stair or 2 slabs from one cut block.
secret: A double slab drops two slabs. Two slabs on top of each other in the crafting grid make the chiseled block of the metal.

lore: {name}: the plain block cut into neat panels, like cut copper that never turns green.
use: Four storage blocks in a square make 4; the stonecutter cuts 4 from one block. It breaks and resists like its storage block and drops itself.
secret: Six of them make 4 stairs, three make 6 slabs, four in a square make 4 tiles. The stonecutter turns one into a stair, two slabs, a tile block or a chiseled block.

lore: {name}: a floor of small metal squares, each one catching the light a little differently.
use: Four cut blocks in a square make 4; the stonecutter gives 4 from a storage block or 1 from a cut block. Decoration; it breaks like its storage block and drops itself.
secret: Unlike copper blocks they never oxidise and need no wax.

lore: {name}: a column of metal that holds its line.
use: Two storage blocks on top of each other make 2; the stonecutter cuts 1 from a block. Placed along an axis like the quartz pillar. It breaks like its storage block and drops itself.
secret: Lay it on its side for a beam: the pattern follows the axis you place it on.

lore: {name}: a showpiece metal with an emblem cut into it.
use: The stonecutter cuts it 1:1 from the block of its metal; like the netherite block there is no cut family. Needs a diamond pickaxe, fire resistant, decoration only.
secret: The motifs: an Eye of Ender for Enderite, a tree for Terranite, a Ghast for Infernite, a sun for Zenithite. Unlike its block it is no beacon base.

lore: {name}: a square of metal with a motif struck into its face.
use: Two cut slabs of the metal on top of each other make 1; the stonecutter cuts 4 from a storage block or 1 from a cut block. Decoration only; it breaks like its storage block.
secret: Each metal strikes its own motif: rose gold shows a rose, rose copper a heart.

lore: {name}: iron bars that chose another metal and a pattern of their own.
use: Six ingots in two rows make 16. They join each other, panes and walls like iron bars, count as Vanilla bars and let light and view through. Any pickaxe.
secret: Every metal draws its own pattern: lead in thick round rods, silver in fine tendrils, brass in rhombs. Unlike copper they never age.

lore: {name}: a lattice of metal, see-through and steady.
use: Four storage blocks in a diamond make 4, or the stonecutter makes 4 from one block, like the copper grate. See-through, and it can hold water. Needs a stone pickaxe.
secret: It does not age and needs no wax: only copper oxidises. Its pattern is the one you see in the window of the metal's door and the cage of its lamp.

lore: {name}: a hatch of metal that opens at a touch.
use: Four ingots (2 x 2) make 1. It opens by hand or by redstone like the copper trapdoor. Any pickaxe.
secret: It carries the same grate pattern as the door of its metal, so door and hatch match. Nothing about it ages.

lore: {name}: a metal door with a window of its own grate pattern.
use: Six ingots (2 x 3) make 3. It opens by hand or by redstone like the copper door, and villagers and other mobs use it. Any pickaxe.
secret: The window shows the metal's grate pattern, the frame its tones. It never ages, so it looks the same in a hundred years.

lore: {name}: a lamp that remembers whether you last told it on or off.
use: Works like the copper bulb: each redstone pulse switches it on or off, it stays as it is without power, light 15. Three storage blocks, a blaze rod and redstone make 4. Stone pickaxe.
secret: A comparator reads 15 while it is on, so it doubles as a memory cell. The cage shows the metal's grate pattern and never ages.

lore: {name}: a small light in a metal house.
use: Like the Vanilla lantern: it stands on a block or hangs below one or from a chain, light 15, and can be waterlogged. Eight nuggets of the metal round a torch make 1. Any pickaxe.
secret: Hang it from a chain of the same metal: housing, panes and links then share one style.

lore: {name}: links of metal, each shaped by its own maker.
use: A nugget, an ingot and a nugget upright make 1. Like the iron chain it is placed along any axis, holds lanterns and can be waterlogged. Any pickaxe.
secret: Every metal shapes its links differently; a chain and a lantern of one metal belong together.

lore: {name}: a slim rod of metal, standing tall for the look of it.
use: Three ingots upright make 1. Placed like the lightning rod on the side you click, and it can be waterlogged. Needs a stone pickaxe. Decoration only.
secret: Lightning ignores it: only the copper rod and the iron, gold, emerald, diamond, netherite and enderite poles draw strikes.

lore: {name}: a light plate that counts every visitor.
use: Two ingots side by side make 1. A weighted pressure plate like the gold one: one signal level per entity on it, up to 15. Any pickaxe.
secret: Precious metals count fine: use it where a single item or mob should already change the signal.

lore: {name}: a heavy plate that waits for a crowd.
use: Two ingots side by side make 1. A weighted pressure plate like the iron one: one signal level per 10 entities, full strength at 150. Any pickaxe.
secret: The plate shows the block of its metal, so it disappears into a floor of the same material.

lore: {name}: a crumb of metal, small enough to lose in a pocket.
use: Nine make an ingot of the metal, and an ingot gives nine back. Lanterns, chains and the rose gold carrots are made from nuggets.
secret: Some finds come as nuggets: End silver ore drops silver nuggets, tin-bearing gravel and sand drop tin nuggets. Rift metal nuggets are fire resistant.

lore: {name}: a tool as quick as gold that does not give up as fast.
use: Crafted from Rose Gold ingots like the Vanilla tool. Mines like iron, speed 12 like gold, durability 225 (iron 250), enchantability 22. Repair with Rose Gold ingots.
secret: It is the better of the two alloys: faster than iron and much easier to enchant. With Simple Hammers installed rose gold also gets a sledgehammer.

lore: {name}: a copper-rose tool, sturdy enough for a day's work.
use: Crafted from Rose Copper ingots like the Vanilla tool. Mines like iron, speed 8, durability 190 like copper, enchantability 15. Repair with Rose Copper ingots.
secret: Weaker than Rose Gold despite the richer recipe: choose it for the color. With Simple Hammers installed it also gets a sledgehammer.

lore: {name}: armor with a pale pink shine.
use: Crafted from Rose Gold ingots like Vanilla armor. Protection 2/5/3/1 for helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots, durability like iron (factor 15), enchantability 25.
secret: Enchantability 25 like gold, yet it lasts as long as iron: good armor to enchant.

lore: {name}: armor in a darker copper-rose.
use: Crafted from Rose Copper ingots like Vanilla armor. Protection 2/4/3/1 like copper armor, durability factor 11, enchantability 12.
secret: Rose Gold armor is stronger in every number; Rose Copper armor is a look, not an upgrade.

lore: {name}: a long reach in rose-coloured metal.
use: Crafted like the Vanilla spear from two sticks and an alloy ingot. Rose Copper: copper spear timing, durability 190, enchantability 15. Rose Gold: golden spear timing with the iron damage factor, durability 225, enchantability 22. Repair with the alloy ingot.
secret: Charge it like any spear: the faster you move, the harder the hit.

lore: {name}: rose metal for a mount.
use: Horse armor: seven alloy ingots in the leather horse armor shape. Nautilus armor: eight alloy ingots around a nautilus shell. Body armor 4 (Rose Copper, like copper) or 6 (Rose Gold, between iron and gold); enchantability 12 or 25.
secret: Vanilla metal horse armor is only found, never crafted; the alloys are the exception.

lore: {name}: forged from netherite, it carries the End inside the metal.
use: Smithing table: Enderite Upgrade, the netherite tool and an Enderite ingot. Durability 2530 (netherite 2031), mining speed 10, enchantability 18. Repair with Enderite ingots.
secret: Fire resistant and safe from the void like every Enderite item. Enderite pickaxes are the only pickaxes that break Dimensional Scrap.

lore: {name}: even the mount deserves a coat from the End.
use: Smithing table: Enderite Upgrade, the netherite horse or nautilus armor and an Enderite ingot. 22 armor instead of 19, toughness 4, knockback resistance 0.2.
secret: No durability, and it can be sheared off like the Vanilla one. Fire resistant, safe from the void, and a dropped one lasts twice as long.

lore: {name}: a shell for those who intend to fall a long way and walk away.
use: Smithing table: Enderite Upgrade, the netherite piece and an Enderite ingot. One armor point more than netherite (4/9/7/4), toughness 4, knockback resistance 0.2, enchantability 18.
secret: Fire resistant, safe from the void, and it carries armor trims like any Vanilla armor.

lore: {name}: a golden carrot that went a little pink.
use: 8 nuggets of the alloy round a carrot, like the golden carrot. Rose Copper carrot 7 hunger, Rose Gold carrot 8, saturation factor 1.2 (golden carrot: 6 hunger). No effects.
secret: Nuggets, not ingots: eight ingots would make a carrot as dear as an apple. There is no enchanted version.

lore: {name}: the dimension's apple, given a glow.
use: Eight ingots of the metal round its apple. 6 hunger, always edible. Regeneration II 0:20, Absorption IV 2:00, Resistance I 5:00 and 5:00 of the metal's effect (Haste, Fire Resistance or Slow Falling).
secret: Fire resistant like the ingots, and glinting. Five minutes of help for mining, the Nether or the End islands.

lore: {name}: a golden apple that took one gift from its dimension.
use: A golden apple and an ingot of the metal, shapeless. 6 hunger, always edible. Regeneration II 0:05, Absorption I 2:00, plus 2:00 of the metal's effect: Terranite Haste, Infernite Fire Resistance, Zenithite Slow Falling.
secret: Fire resistant like the ingots. Eight ingots of the metal round it make the enchanted version.

lore: {name}: a carrot with a pinch of a dimension in it.
use: Eight golden carrots round an ingot of the metal make 8. 8 hunger like the Rose Gold carrot, plus 1:00 of the metal's effect: Terranite Haste, Infernite Fire Resistance, Zenithite Slow Falling.
secret: Fire resistant like the ingots. One ingot makes eight carrots, the cheapest way to carry the effect.

lore: {name}: nine dust that never stop speaking their line.
use: Nine of the line's redstone make one, and one gives the nine back. A permanent source like the redstone block: signal 15 to every side, and pistons push it.
secret: It feeds dust of its own line and Bridge Redstone only (the Bridge block feeds all three lines), but every device next to it reacts.

lore: {name}: a redstone torch that keeps its answer within the family.
use: The line's redstone over a stick makes one. Like the redstone torch it is an inverter: it goes out while its block is powered by any line, glows with light 7 and strongly powers the block above.
secret: Its output belongs to its line: dust of its own line and Bridge Redstone take it, other dust stays dark, devices react. Toggled too often, it burns out.

lore: {name}: dust that climbs where redstone would fall off.
use: Placed by using Astral or Bridge Redstone on the side or the underside of a block; it drops the floor dust. It carries the signal like floor dust and goes round the edge of its block to the next face.
secret: It powers the block it sticks to strongly and connects to floor dust of its line at the edge. Plain redstone dust stays on the floor.

lore: {name}: a component that found a wall to stand on.
use: Placed with the normal item on the side or underside of a block where the floor version cannot stand, or anywhere while sneaking; it drops that item. The output points away from you in the plane of the wall.
secret: Right-click sets the delay, mode or stage as usual. The wall repeater does not lock; the wall comparator reads a container directly behind it.

lore: {name}: an End rod that took on the colors of its line.
use: A blaze rod over Astralit Dust or a Nihilit Shard makes 4. It behaves exactly like the End rod: light 14, sparks at its tip, placed facing away from the clicked face, mined instantly.
secret: Astralit: a white-pink crystal rod on a dark pink base. Nihilit: a pale cyan rod around a dark middle on a teal base.

lore: {name}: a lamp that listens to every line.
use: A redstone lamp and Astral or Nihil Redstone, shapeless. It takes every redstone line and toggles like a copper bulb: each rising signal switches it on or off, light 15.
secret: It is no conductor and relays nothing, so a lamp never leaks a signal from one line into another.
